title: Unveiling contrasting impacts of heat mitigation and adaptation policies on U.S. internal migration
summary: This academic paper studies how heat-related policies affect internal migration across U.S. counties. The researchers analyzed 4,713 heat policies and found that heat adaptation policies (APs) reduce out-migration while heat mitigation policies (MPs) increase it, with heterogeneous effects based on policy type and demographic factors.
key_points: Studied 4,713 heat-related policies and 11,177 migration flows between U.S. counties
Heat adaptation policies (APs) reduce out-migration from affected areas
Heat mitigation policies (MPs) increase out-migration from affected areas
Behavioral and cultural MPs at origins increase annual outflows by 0.24%-0.68% per policy
Behavioral and cultural APs at destinations elevate origin outflows by 0.11%-1.55% per policy
Migration patterns are moderated nonlinearly by income, aging, education, and racial diversity
